content.comment_body: I noticed that the cursor key input works only when accessed from the web interface, but does not function through the physical keys on the [product_name] base module’s front panel, even if the program is running. As a simple test, connecting a counter directly to the cursor key input produced the same result. How can I use the front panel cursor keys as input? Any advice would be appreciated.
If you wish to control the program using the cursor keys, you should press ESC along with the corresponding cursor key.
That is the method I tried, but it only works through the web interface, not with the physical keys on the base module.

This is the first time I've heard of such a situation. The cursor keys work from the web server display, but not with the actual device's keys? In that case, it’s possible the device has a fault, though that's unlikely. These FS:03 base modules are relatively new. Have you tried using a different unit for testing?
All other TS:02 modules are currently undergoing long-term tests, so I cannot interrupt them. Once testing is complete, I will try using another device.

I’ve found out how to utilize the cursor keys in the [product_name] program from the main module. You need to enter the parameter assignment mode (screens), where you’ll find a screen dedicated to cursor keys. Pressing ESC and a cursor key together activates the program’s cursor key function.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered an issue where physical cursor keys on the [product_name] FS:03 base module did not act as expected inputs, only working via the web interface. The confusion stemmed from unclear instructions for hardware interaction, which was clarified after guidance on entering parameter assignment mode and required key combinations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the front panel cursor keys to work as programmable inputs for control purposes, similar to their functionality via the web interface, without needing hidden or complex steps.
